goal: The five-minute invoice job lists a store only when an invoice or credit note can be issued for it now, the store that waited longest first, calls the credit-note function once, and an owner who saves the missing seller details gets the waiting invoices at once; a live drill can prove one invoice end to end.
why: Today the job calls commerce.issue_waiting_invoices and then commerce.issue_missing_credit_notes for the same waiting stores every five minutes for 120 days: about 127 calls of each a day and no invoice issued. After: fewer than 10 calls a day on today's data, and no second call for credit notes.

commits.title: The invoice job asks only stores it can issue for, the longest-waiting first, and calls the credit notes once

changes.how: (1) storesWithDocumentWork(): rewrite the statement so each of its four branches also gives the moment its work began, and the outer query orders by it. Exact shape: select store_id from ( <branch 1> union all <branch 2> union all <branch 3> union all <branch 4> ) x group by store_id order by min(at), store_id limit ${limit}. Branch 1 (orders): `select o.store_id, o.placed_at as at from commerce.orders o left join commerce.invoice_settings cfg on cfg.store_id = o.store_id where` every condition it has today, plus two more at the end: `and commerce.invoice_eligibility(o.id) = 'ok' and commerce.invoice_readiness(o.id) = 'ready'`. Above the two lines write the comment: '-- The same two tests commerce.waiting_invoices() makes before issue_waiting_invoices() issues (reason invoice_failed): a store whose orders wait for its seller details or tax profile is not asked every five minutes (bloat review step 0.30). Keep them the same as that function.' Branch 2 (refunds): today's select with `rf.created_at as at` added to the select list. Branch 3 (order edits): `select e.store_id, coalesce(e.applied_at, e.created_at) as at from commerce.order_edits e where e.status = 'applied' and e.documents = 'waiting'`. Branch 4 (returns refunded outside): today's select with `rt.created_at as at` added. Change `union` to `union all` between them (the outer group by removes duplicates). Keep the SQL comment on branch 3. (2) Split issueWaitingInvoices(): add a private `async function issueWaiting(storeId: string, limit: number): Promise<number | null>` that holds today's body but returns null in the catch (after the same log line); the exported `issueWaitingInvoices(storeId, limit = PER_STORE)` becomes `return (await issueWaiting(storeId, limit)) ?? 0;` so every caller and test sees what it sees today. (3) invoiceJobs(): replace the two lines in the loop with: `const issued = await issueWaiting(storeId, PER_STORE); if (issued === null) await issueMissingCreditNotes(storeId); else result.invoices += issued;` and the comment '// commerce.issue_waiting_invoices() ends by issuing the missing credit notes itself; the second call is only for a store whose invoices failed, so its credit notes do not wait on them.' (4) Update the doc comment of storesWithDocumentWork(): 'a paid order of the last days that has no invoice and can be issued one now (invoicing on, not copied, not a host's, eligible and ready), ...; the stores whose work is oldest first.' Keep issueMissingCreditNotes() exported: the owner's Check again (src/app/admin/(gated)/[store]/invoices/actions.ts) and tests call it.

(a) In the existing case that makes the store `wait` (rg -n 'iss-wait|const wait' src/server/invoice-issue.int.test.ts; it pays an order while the seller's details are missing): directly after the line `expect(await issue.issueWaitingInvoices(wait.storeId)).toBe(0);` and before the `update commerce.stores set legal_name` line add `expect(await issue.storesWithDocumentWork(1000)).not.toContain(wait.storeId);`. In the next case (the store `noProfile`): after the first `expect((await inv.waitingInvoices(noProfile.storeId))[0]).toMatchObject({ reason: "tax_profile_missing" ...` line add `expect(await issue.storesWithDocumentWork(1000)).not.toContain(noProfile.storeId);`. (b) Add a new case 'a store whose orders wait for the seller's details is not picked, and does not keep an issuable store out (bloat review 0.30)': make three stores the way the `wait` store is made (same fixture call and options, names 'iss-q1', 'iss-q2', 'iss-q3'), pay one order in each in that order (q1 first). Then give q1 and q2 their details with the same `update commerce.stores set legal_name = ..., organisation_number = ..., postal_address = ..., country = 'NO'` statement the `wait` case uses; leave q3 waiting. `const list = await issue.storesWithDocumentWork(1000);` expect list to contain q1 and q2, not q3, and `list.indexOf(q1.storeId)` to be less than `list.indexOf(q2.storeId)` (the longest-waiting first). (c) Add a case 'the job issues the invoices and calls the credit notes once': with the pg.Client spy (copy `counted()` from src/server/variants-scale.int.test.ts lines 96 to 105, returning the statements' texts), run `await issue.invoiceJobs()` and expect: no statement contains 'issue_missing_credit_notes', q1 and q2 now have an invoice (`fx.invoiceOf`), q3 has none, and no statement containing 'issue_waiting_invoices' has q3's store id among its values. If invoiceJobs() makes network calls in this fixture (ensureSubscriptionEvents, reconcilePendingRefunds), look at how another case of this file or of src/server/invoice-refunds.int.test.ts runs invoiceJobs() and stub the same things. Leave line `expect(await issue.storesWithDocumentWork()).toContain(wait.storeId);` as it is unless it fails only because more than 50 older stores are ahead in the shared database: then, and only then, pass 1000.
